slides.say: Children can be text, numbers, elements, or nothing at all. Two types cover them, and they're not the same.
React dot React Node is the broad one: everything you can put between JSX tags, including strings and numbers. It's the usual choice.
React Element is narrower: only JSX elements. A plain string like hello is rejected.

slides.text: Limit: TypeScript can't say “only <li> children”. Any JSX element passes the check.
slides.say: One limit. TypeScript can't require a specific kind of element, like only list items. Any JSX element passes.
